newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian university awards Suu Kyi honorary degree.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian university awards Suu Kyi honorary degree.

text.p: An Australian university on Friday awarded Burma's Aung San Suu Kyi an honorary doctorate, a move which Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said demonstrated Australia's respect for the pro-democracy leader.
Sydney's University of Technology said it had awarded Suu Kyi an honorary Doctorate of Letters in recognition of her role in Burma's pro-democracy movement and her commitment to human rights.
Suu Kyi's husband, Michael Aris, received the award as she was unable to leave Burma because of government restrictions on her movements.
In a speech delivered on her behalf, Aris said Suu Kyi wanted young Australians to remember Burma's struggle and to recognise her country's need for information.
"Australians, as the citizens of a nation forged out of hard endeavour, have a reputation for a tough, independent mentality," Aris said for Suu Kyi.
"We expect from you the boldness to stand up and speak for the rights of those who are seeking to cast off their shackles."
Downer said in a statement the award was a sign of the respect Australians had for Suu Kyi "and the struggle that she represents".
Downer said he had repeatedly called for Burma's State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) to end political repression in Burma and to release all political prisoners.

He also called for Burma to make a meaningful transition to civilian government through genuine negotiations between the government, Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy and ethnic minority representatives.
"I will continue to take all practical steps to encourage the development of democracy and a greater respect for human rights in Burma," he said on Suu Kyi's behalf.
Suu Kyi has often called for international sanctions on Burma's SLORC as a result of human rights abuses.
The SLORC seized power in 1988 and ignored the results of subsequent elections won by Suu Kyi's party.
